Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory white paper LLNL-TR-2012486, by Peter Lindstrom, dated October 2025, tackles a data handling flaw in the zfp compression library. Zfp squeezes numerical arrays by exploiting how smoothly values vary across space. Real data sets also carry special values: infinities, not-a-number markers, and fill values that flag missing data, common in earth science files.

Left alone, a fill value poisons its neighborhood during compression, blurring the true values around it. The paper proposes several ways for zfp to recognize special values without breaking files written by older versions. One scheme repurposes an unused code path; its cost is a reserved exponent worth 8 or 11 bits per affected block, a price the author calls high. Workarounds for current users close the paper, so the fix can be weighed before it lands.
